Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned (2209.07858v1) · paper method: The authors state that they do not know whether crowdworkers have expertise needed to assess some technical harms and that attack coverage is incomplete; the review workflow includes warnings, opt-out previews, support communication and a voluntary well-being survey.

cohort3.claim.redteam.coverage-expertise-limits

  • This assertion originated as an author proposal; separate review receipts determine its current status.
  • Version-specific author-reported study; experiments, raw dataset records and formal proofs were not independently reproduced or verified.
  • Worker-support descriptions do not establish absence of harm, and reduced average harmfulness does not establish a perfectly safe model.

Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned (2209.07858v1) · paper method: Self-reported attack success shows no clear model-size trend, while minimum harmlessness-model scores show RLHF models becoming harder to red-team with scale; harmful outputs still occur.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned (2209.07858v1) · paper method: At each dialogue turn, participants see two model responses and select the more harmful; after the conversation they rate attack success on a 0–4 scale, separately from the learned preference-model harmlessness score.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned (2209.07858v1) · paper method: A follow-up sample of 500 attacks each on 52B prompted and RLHF models receives three reviewer ratings per transcript; agreement including the attack author is Fleiss kappa0.32 on Likert ratings and 0.49 after binarization.

Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned (2209.07858v1) · paper method: The study’s red team comprises 324 US-based crowdworkers: 307 recruited through MTurk and 17 through Upwork; about 80% of attacks come from roughly 50 workers.
